description: We are developing a topographic and mathematical navigation concept for safe Marswalks under the Interplanetary Survival Guide challenge.
summary: Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map is a navigation and survival system designed for explorers operating in Jezero Crater on Mars. Because Mars lacks real-time Earth-based GPS and constant network connectivity, astronauts and surface teams face serious risks of losing orientation or communication during missions. Our project solves this problem by providing an offline Martian map paired with peer-to-peer (P2P) communication capabilities. The system allows explorers to navigate safely across Jezero Crater, identify safe routes, and maintain direct local communication with team members without relying on external infrastructure. By prioritizing reliability, simplicity, and offline accessibility, this project enhances mission safety and supports human survival in extreme extraterrestrial environments.
details: What It Does & How It Works: Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map is an offline navigation and communication solution built specifically for Jezero Crater on Mars. It provides explorers with a reliable local map for route planning and hazard awareness without needing an internet connection or satellite GPS. Alongside offline mapping, the concept integrates peer-to-peer (P2P) communication so team members on the Martian surface can share locations, alerts, and critical updates directly with one another. Benefits & Intended Impact: In the harsh environment of Mars, communication delays with Earth and signal blackouts can become life-threatening. Our solution ensures that astronauts and surface teams remain oriented, connected, and safe even when cut off from main base stations. It reduces navigation errors, improves emergency response times, and provides a practical survival tool for future planetary missions. Creativity & Key Considerations: When designing this project, our team focused on real Martian constraints: lack of GPS, communication latency, harsh terrain in Jezero Crater, and the need for an intuitive interface that works under high-stress conditions. Combining offline spatial guidance with decentralized P2P connectivity makes the system resilient, lightweight, and adaptable for future space exploration.
